note: Read: Van Osdel designed two houses on Prairie Avenue; 'The first of these, at 1834 S. Prairie Avenue, was built in 1866 for one of Chicago's earliest pioneers - Fernando Jones'; 'The Italianate style house was razed in 1942.' The photograph, from across the street, shows the house before its 1886 mansard: two storeys of brick on a high stone basement, deep eaves on paired carved brackets, a low pediment-like gable with a round window over the middle of the front, tall windows under curved stone hoods, a one-storey angled bay on the flank, and a stoop with iron railings. T-1888: the print is laterally reversed, as Chicagology's of the same negative is (chicagology_1834_jones_photo): the flank it shows is the north one, and the bay stands 9-14 m back from the front, where the 1911 sheet draws it.
what_it_supplies: the style, the architect and the year built
that the house was razed in 1942
the front and north flank as they stood before 1886: brackets, centre gable, window hoods, flank bay, stoop
what_it_does_not_supply: the 1904 roofline: the photograph predates the mansard
